Namecoin is decentralized DNS built from an early (2011) fork of Bitcoin. It works. Just needs more adoption. With registrars getting into the censorship game, now is a good time to consider it.

OpenNIC.org runs normal DNS servers that also allow domains unregulated by ICANN (.bbs .dyn .geek .null .pirate and a few others). Almost all the OpenNIC servers will work for normal domains, OpenNICs' own top levels, and most will also resolve Namecoins' (.bit). While placing DNS in a blockchain does decentralize it, it also doesn't work with normal software. The best of both worlds seems to be placing namecoin behind a unregulated group of DNS servers.

Services like OpenNIC are the next logical step. OpenNIC even supports .bit domains through a Namecoin proxy. That way if people really prefer .bit, then you can still run it with traditional DNS through OpenNIC. That's easiest solution for end-users at this moment (all they need to do is install the OpenNIC app, and they are set).
